title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/22/2026

Reason for Admission: Sepsis and pneumonia.

Vitals: BP 118/72, HR 88, SpO2 96% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.
Recent Labs: WBC 14.5 x 10^9/L, Lactate 2.1 mmol/L, Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, BUN 18 mg/dL, Hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL.

HPI: Patient is a 55-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with a three-day history of productive cough, shortness of breath, and high-grade fever. He reported significant pleuritic chest pain and generalized malaise. He denied any recent travel or known exposures. He was started on initial fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fever, chills, and fatigue.
Respiratory: Positive for cough and dyspnea. Negative for wheezing.
Cardiovascular: Negative for palpitations or edema.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea or diarrhea.
Neurological: Negative for headache or confusion.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain.

Social History: Lives with wife in a private residence. Works as a technician. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.
Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.
Hospital Course: The patient was admitted for severe pneumonia. His clinical status deteriorated rapidly, leading to the development of septic shock. He required the initiation of vasopressors to maintain adequate mean arterial pressure. He was treated with aggressive fluid resuscitation and intravenous antibiotics. Despite the severity of the septic shock, he responded well to treatment. Cultures remained negative for specific growth. His oxygen requirements decreased steadily, and he was successfully weaned off vasopressors. He remained stable for 48 hours before being cleared for discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Pneumonia
Sepsis
Septic shock

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin 875mg every 8 hours (7 days)
Albuterol inhaler as needed
Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for fever

Follow-up: Patient to follow up with primary care physician in 7 days for wound check and respiratory status.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, MD, 05/22/2026
explanations: Septic shock is severe sepsis with circulatory failure: A41.9 plus R65.21.

distractors.why: Septic shock is documented: R65.21, not R65.20.

style.document: Write a hospital discharge summary with sections: Admission Date, Discharge Date, Reason for Admission, Hospital Course, Discharge Diagnoses, Discharge Medications, Follow-up. It is the inpatient record of this hospital stay, not an office note.
